title: Open Agentic Platform — compiled spec registry (deterministic MVP)

inputRoot.description: Repository-relative root used for this compilation. Canonical full-repo value is "."; normalization rules: Feature 000 research D8 and Feature 001 spec.

domain.description: Spec 179 — tract-authority lens. Closed enum; V-030 validates membership at error severity.

amends.description: Spec 132 — IDs of specs this spec amends. Companion to `amendsSections`.

amendsSections.description: Spec 132 — section anchors this spec claims to amend in the specs named in `amends`. V-011 rejects any anchor that appears in the amended spec's `unamendable` list.

unamendable.description: Spec 132 — section anchors that future amendments cannot touch. An amending spec referencing one of these via `amendsSections` produces V-011.

shape.description: Spec 147 — kind-refinement. Validated against the declared (kind, shape) table; novel pairs surface W-131 from spec-lint.

category.description: Spec 147 — cross-cutting tag list. Unconventional values surface W-130 from spec-lint.

supersedes.description: Spec 147/130/216: specs this spec replaces. An item is a bare spec-id string (full-scope shorthand) or a `{spec, scope, unit?, note?, rationale?}` object (spec 216 Phase 2a). Full-scope objects normalise to bare strings at emission; partial-scope objects carry the per-unit (or prose `note:`) scope of the authority transfer.

supersededBy.description: Spec 147 — successor spec id; V-019 enforces presence and resolution when status=superseded.

retirementRationale.description: Spec 147 — structured retirement record; V-018 enforces presence when status=retired.

implements.description: Spec 147 — either a scalar registry-id (kind=capability) or a list of {path, primary?} code-path claims. V-014 enforces shape consistency; V-015 enforces registry resolution; V-016 enforces corpus-wide `primary:` uniqueness.

provides.description: Spec 147 — capability contribution declaration; required when kind=capability per V-013.

composition.description: Spec 147 — capability-graph namespace. `composition.requires` is required by V-013 for kind=capability and kind=profile.

selectableBy.description: Spec 147 — env var name selecting this capability among alternatives. V-015 verifies equality with target registry's selector when present.

selector.description: Spec 147 — required when kind=registry per V-013. Env var consumers use to pick an implementation.

default.description: Spec 147 — optional default for registry selector when no value is provided.

productionForbidden.description: Spec 147 — selector values forbidden in production environments.

memberContract.description: Spec 147 — required when kind=registry per V-013. Spec id or trait name that registry members must satisfy.

identity.description: Spec 147 — required when kind=profile per V-013. Structured tenant identity record.

selects.description: Spec 147 — required when kind=profile per V-013. Map of registry-spec-id → capability-spec-id. V-017 enforces validity.

policy.description: Spec 147 — optional structured policy values applied by the profile. Compile-time validation is structural only; semantic validation lives in the policy-kernel.

establishes.description: Spec 130 (relationship graph) — code paths this spec brought into existence. Authoritative on those paths until superseded. Items may be a bare path string (legacy / `file:` unit) or a `{unit: <logical-unit>}` object (spec 154).

extends.description: Spec 130 — extensions to another spec's authority surface. Each item references the predecessor spec, the subset of its surface this spec extends, and the nature (additive | wrapping).

refines.description: Spec 130 — refinements that tighten behavior across paths. Each item carries an aspect tag and optionally lists the specs it refines.

coAuthority.description: Spec 130 — co-authority on a named section of a shared path. The diff-to-section matcher lives in spec 152 (path-co-authority).

constrains.description: Spec 130 — meta-authority over how others may shape code. Constraint specs are not behavior authorities; the gate evaluates them separately.

origin.description: Spec 130 — bootstrap or retroactive marker. `retroactive: true` indicates the spec's `implements:` carries forward as its surface without curated relationship annotation.

references.description: Spec 154 — ninth relationship, declaratively non-owning. Items are units the spec mentions for evidence / illustration / provenance without claiming authority. The coupling gate ignores `references:`; the codebase-indexer surfaces them for navigation.

implementsItem.description: Spec 147 — one entry in `implements:` list form.

extendsItem.description: Spec 130 — one entry in `extends:`. Spec 154 added optional `unit:` for typed logical-unit ownership; the legacy `paths:` form remains valid.

refinesItem.description: Spec 130 — one entry in `refines:`. Spec 154 added optional `unit:`; either `paths:` (legacy) or `unit:` (new) is acceptable, but at least one of them must be present in addition to `aspect`.

coAuthorityItem.description: Spec 130/152 — one entry in `co_authority:`. `section` names a per-file-type anchor (Makefile target group, markdown heading, workflow jobs.<name>, source-file `// region: <name>`). Spec 154 added optional `unit:` for the new section-unit form; either the legacy (`paths` + `section`) pair or the new `unit:` is acceptable.

constrainsItem.description: Spec 130 — one entry in `constrains:`. The relationship-level discriminator is `kind:` (legacy) or `flavor:` (spec 154 §5 — renamed to free `kind:` for `unit.kind`); both are accepted during the compat window. Authors target either code paths (`paths:`) or other specs (`target_specs:`); `spec:` is the single-target shorthand. Spec 154 also added optional `unit:` for the new unit-typed form.

target_specs.description: Spec 130 — list of spec ids this constraint targets. Use when the constraint applies to several specs as peers rather than to code paths or a single spec.

logicalUnit.description: Spec 154 — one logical-unit declaration. Six kinds capture the observed ownership shapes across the corpus (crate, symbol, module, section, directory, file). The `crate:` kind binds the workspace-member manifest name; spec-compiler validates that name against the root Cargo.toml [workspace] members (V-021). `directory:` and `file:` paths are validated against worktree existence (V-022, V-023). Symbol / module / section anchor resolution is deferred to the codebase-indexer (Tier 2 Segment 3).

relationshipUnitItem.description: Spec 154 — relationship-list item carrying a logical unit. Used for `establishes:` items written in the new typed shape.

supersedeScopedItem.description: Spec 130/154/216 Phase 2a: a structured `supersedes:` entry. `scope: full` normalises to a bare spec-id string at emission, so only `scope: partial` entries persist as objects. A partial entry scopes the authority transfer by `unit:` (a logical unit) or by a prose `note:`; `unit:` is not required.

referenceItem.description: Spec 154 — one entry in `references:`. Three accepted shapes: bare path string (legacy / hand-authored shorthand), `{role?, unit: <logical-unit>}` (spec 154 canonical), or `{role?, provenance: {kind, ref}}` (spec 156 — typed external derivation pointer, mutually exclusive with `unit:` per V-025). The optional `role:` is open-vocabulary and presentation-only — the coupling gate treats every `references:` item uniformly as non-owning.

provenanceEntry.description: Spec 156 — typed external derivation pointer. Two initial kinds: `knowledge` (statecraft `knowledge_objects` URI shape) and `code-fingerprint` (xray content-addressed SHA-256). Adding a new kind requires an amendment spec that widens both this enum and V-027's scheme alignment table.

ref.description: URI matching the declared kind's scheme. `knowledge`: `statecraft://project/<uuid>/knowledge/<uuid>`; `code-fingerprint`: `xray-fingerprint://<sha256>`. Scheme alignment is enforced at compile time by V-027; body well-formedness by V-028.

extraFrontmatterValue.description: Scalar or string-list only; no nested objects or heterogeneous arrays.
